reading: The proposal would change one recorded function. The link from a declined share to the Lowfen channel would drain the share first into its household's own holding, with only excess running down the lowest Lowfen terrace (E12, E4), as the selected alternative (E2) and the instruction (E1) describe. The Source still follows balance (E18), the rota record is unchanged (E32), and the Lowfen channel's wording is identical (E28), but that wording would then cover only excess. On this reading, the refusal's wild-water cost shifts from the lower valley's wells toward the refusing household, and the size of that shift depends on a holding capacity the record does not give. Reach is not established: no indexed Book element cites the changed link.

concerns.title: Refusal drains first into the refuser's own holding
concerns.earlier: A declined share's unkept water runs wild down the lowest Lowfen terrace.
concerns.proposed: A declined share drains first into its household's own holding; only the excess runs down the lowest Lowfen terrace.
concerns.reading: The proposed link function would give the refusing household's own holding the first flow of a declined share's unkept water, so that the lowest Lowfen terrace receives only what the holding cannot take. The change is stated only as the link's function, as the instruction asks, and is developed from the selected alternative's text.
counterevidence: The holding's capacity, layout and location are not recorded as a node, so the routing rests on the link's wording alone.

concerns.title: Lower valley's wild-water exposure may be displaced
concerns.earlier: The lowest Lowfen terrace is where a declined share's water runs wild, in the channel that carries Lower Ammen's wells.
concerns.reading: The lower valley's exposure to a refusal's full wild water may move onto the refusing household's own holding, because only excess would reach the lowest terrace. Whether it moves depends on the holding's capacity, which the record does not give, so the concern is reduced or displaced rather than removed.
counterevidence: Only excess reaches the lowest terrace, so the exposure is reduced rather than removed.
The record does not say how often a declined share occurs, so the scale of the exposure is unknown.
concerns.competing_reading: Read as a reduction rather than a displacement: the same terrace still takes the excess, so the lower wells keep part of the exposure.

trajectories.title: Refusal's first loss stays in the refuser's household

steps.text: If a household declines its share from the rota, the proposed link would drain its unkept water first into its own holding.
Only the excess the holding cannot take would run down the lowest Lowfen terrace, which E28 names as the place of wild water.
The refusing household's own fields and well take the first loss, a cost of declining that falls on the one who declined.
The page could show the holding flooding as a named household's consequence of the kind E24 records.

assumptions: The holding's capacity is set by the author, since the record does not give it.
The page shows the refusing household's own holding.

comparison.creative_gain: A named, physical cost of refusal that stays within one household.
comparison.narrative_cost: The lower valley's wild-water threat recedes, weakening a Lowfen-based stake in refusal.
comparison.contrivance_risk: A holding that floods only when refused may read as punishment rather than physics.
comparison.future_commitment: Commits the link's routing and needs the holding's capacity recorded later.
comparison.flexibility: The link can return to its baseline function (E12) without changing any node.

trajectories.title: Lower terrace exposed when the holding is full

steps.text: If a refusal occurs while the refuser's holding still has room, the lowest terrace stays dry from that share.
A share larger than the holding would send its excess down the Lowfen as the baseline did, so the lower wells meet wild water in that case.

assumptions: The holding's capacity is finite and not yet recorded.

alternatives.title: Keep the wild water running down the lowest terrace
alternatives.summary: Keep the link's recorded function, so a declined share's unkept water runs wild down the lowest Lowfen terrace as the baseline states. The proposed change is not adopted, and the refusing household is not placed first in the physical cost.
alternatives.gains: Keeps the lower valley's cost exactly as recorded, and leaves the Lowfen wording and the spring's routing unchanged.
alternatives.costs: The lower wells meet the full wild water of a refusal, and the refusal drain the instruction asks for is not developed.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether the Book 19 break of the Lowfen (E28) involved wild water before choosing a routing.

alternatives.title: Adopt the refuser-first drain as written
alternatives.summary: Take the proposed link function as written: a declined share drains first into its household's own holding, and only the excess runs down the lowest Lowfen terrace. Choosing this would record the lower valley's displacement as accepted, not resolved; nothing is accepted here.
alternatives.gains: Places the first loss on the refusing household and spares the lowest terrace except for excess, so declining becomes a visible physical choice.
alternatives.costs: The holding has no recorded node or capacity, so the excess threshold is undetermined, and the lower valley's exposure is displaced rather than removed.
alternatives.next_investigation: Decide whether the holding needs its own recorded node or only the link's function before any finale is considered.

alternatives.title: Hold the routing until the holding is specified
alternatives.summary: Postpone reconsideration of the routing and keep the baseline link (E12) as it stands until the holding's capacity and layout are recorded, or until the author decides whether a holding node is wanted.
alternatives.gains: Avoids fixing an unrecorded capacity into the link and keeps the recorded wild-water wording intact.
alternatives.costs: The refusal drain stays undeveloped, and the open question of the holding's capacity stays unanswered.
alternatives.next_investigation: Name the evidence that would settle it: a recorded capacity for the household's holding, or an author decision on whether a holding node is wanted.

alternatives.title: Answer the refusal's first loss with the rota's labour
alternatives.summary: Hold the refusal routing (E12) and the rota's labour record (E32) in one development, so that a flooded holding is answered together with who can return labour. The combined development gives up a purely physical account of a refusal's cost.
alternatives.gains: Connects a refusal's cost to the labour that keeps the channels, which the rota record already ties to households that can meet it.
alternatives.costs: Gives up a purely physical account of refusal, and the link from a flooded holding to labour is not recorded.
alternatives.next_investigation: Establish whether a flood on a holding reduces the household's rota labour, which the record does not say.
